title: Operational at scale: discovery past the peer map, retention as a contract, machine-readable refusals
description:
Mark, 2026-11-22: "operational, not protocol."

DISCOVERY, the quiet one. mimid finds peers through a CONFIGURED PEER
MAP, not DNS: config.rs says "It replaces DNS discovery (decision
mimid-1wgh.17)", and the live host proves the shape, with Haven added by
hand this session as one line of TOML. That is fine for one Haven and
untenable for "all of them". The work is bead mimid-1wgh.37.94 (which
host serves a provider's directory, raised with the WG and unsent) plus
real §5.1 discovery. Note the mandate makes this worse than a
convenience problem: a configured map means a human decision per peer,
and an obligation to interoperate with all comers does not allow one.

RETENTION BECOMES A CONTRACT. Today `message_retention_secs` is an
operator setting, 7 days by default (decision mimid-1wgh.82). Follower
catch-up (mimid-1wgh.37.104) turns it into a promise to other
providers: the design note ties the catch-up window to exactly that
setting, so shortening retention shortens what a peer can recover, and
a peer that was down longer loses messages permanently. Under a mandate
that is a term someone will want written down, and §6 of the design note
proposes only a SHOULD with a stated minimum.

MACHINE-READABLE REFUSALS. Epic mimid-1wgh.55 (mimi-protocol #190):
structured refusal reasons, retry hints, request extension points. With
one friendly peer a human reads a log; with a hundred peers a refusal
has to be something software can act on. Related and now shipped:
mimid-75nk.12 gives a 403 from provider authentication a `reason`
member, which is the same idea one layer down.
